topic: Photographing a moment can make you remember it less
subject: technology

facts.claim: Taking photos makes people recognize even nonphotographed aspects better than people without a camera.
facts.quote: Furthermore, participants who used a camera during their experience recognized even nonphotographed aspects better than participants without a camera did.

facts.claim: Taking photos makes people remember more of what they saw and less of what they heard compared to those who could not take photographs.
facts.quote: we found that, even without revisiting any photos, participants who could freely take photographs during an experience recognized more of what they saw and less of what they heard, compared with those who could not take any photographs.

facts.claim: Taking photos makes people perform worse on both perceptually driven and conceptually driven memory tests.
facts.quote: Contrary to predictions, the results showed impairment both on perceptually driven and conceptually driven tests, which were found both after a short (20 min) and long (48 h) delay between encoding at test.

facts.claim: Taking photos makes people less likely to remember objects they photograph than objects they only observe.
facts.quote: A photo-taking-impairment effect has been observed such that participants are less likely to remember objects they photograph than objects they only observe.

facts.claim: Taking photos makes people less accurate and less confident in remembering artworks during a mock museum tour.
facts.quote: In Experiment 1 and 3 following intentional encoding, a photo-taking impairment effect impacting accuracy and confidence was observed.

facts.claim: Taking photos makes people perform worse on on-slide information in an in-person learning environment.
facts.quote: Experiment 2 failed to replicate this interaction; there was an overall photo-taking impairment for on-slide information in an in-person learning environment.

research.angle: While taking photos often impairs memory for specific objects or concepts, it can also improve recognition of visual aspects and non-photographed details of an experience.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that photo-taking typically impairs memory for specific items but can simultaneously enhance visual recognition and memory for surrounding context.
research.caveat: The effects of photo-taking vary significantly depending on the environment, such as whether the learning is happening in-person or online.
